statements.t: We are structured as a privately placed, non-listed, perpetual-life REIT, and therefore our securities are not listed on a national securities exchange and, as of the date of this Form 10-Q, there is no plan to list our securities on a national securities exchange.

We are not aware of any material trends or uncertainties, favorable or unfavorable, other than national economic conditions affecting real estate generally, that may be reasonably anticipated to have a material impact on either capital resources or the revenues or income to be derived from investments in our target assets, other than those referred to in the 2025 Form 10-K under Part I, Item 1A.
We will reimburse the Adviser for all such advanced costs and expenses ratably over the 60 months following the end of such advancements.
After the end of such advancements, we will reimburse the Adviser for any organization and offering expenses and operating costs and expenses it incurs on behalf of us as and when incurred.

The declaration of distributions will reduce the NAV for each class of our shares in an amount equal to the accrual of our liability to pay any such distribution to our shareholders of record of each class.
Operating expenses incurred after the first anniversary of the initial closing of our Private Offering will be paid by the Company and deducted as an expense for NAV as incurred.

We expect to generate cash primarily from (i) the net proceeds of our continuous Private Offering, (ii) cash flows from our operations, (iii) existing borrowing facilities and any financing arrangements we may enter into in the future and (iv) any future offerings of our equity or debt securities.

Our primary uses of cash will be for (i) the acquisition of our target assets in accordance with our investment guidelines or ongoing advances related to those initial acquisitions, (ii) the cost of operations (including the management fee and performance fee), (iii) debt service of any borrowings, (iv) periodic repurchases, including under our share repurchase plan, and (v) cash distributions (if any) to the…

An increase in short-term interest rates increases our interest expense on those financings and, to the extent not offset by increases in income on our investments or gains on our economic hedging instruments, may reduce or adversely affect our net interest income and our net asset value.

Increases in SOFR that raise our interest expense on our floating-rate secured financings are expected to be offset in part by gains on the futures positions, and decreases in SOFR that lower our interest expense are expected to be offset in part by losses on the positions.
We expect to continue to hold the positions against our floating-rate secured financings as those financings are repaid, refinanced or replaced.

As a result, gains and losses in the fair value of the position are recognized in our results of operations in the period in which they occur, while the interest expense the positions are intended to offset is recognized over the terms of our floating-rate secured financings as the interest expense accrues.
The Company does not currently anticipate additional advances of such expenses during the extension period.
